summary: Initial security and compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning for FinEdge's plan to deploy Redwood-hosted inference with EU data residency. Discussed region pinning options (hosted vs dedicated EU capacity), cross-border processing exceptions, subprocessors, KMS/encryption, RBAC/SSO, and audit/logging. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, technical region-pinning diagram, and schedule a VPC deep-dive.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (CISO, FinEdge), Marta Lopez (Lead Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Legal), Jenna Rowe (Product)

Summary: Quick security/compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning. Customer wants EU-residency for EU customers, minimize cross-border processing, and clarity on subprocessors and KMS.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, im joined by Priya our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Daniel: Daniel here, CISO at FinEdge. Marta, Samir and Jenna from our side.
[00:15] Marta: Hi all.
[00:20] Priya: Hi, thanks, quick agenda — go over data residency reqs, region pinning options (hosted vs dedicated), subprocessors, and encryption/KMS, and then Q&A and next steps.
[00:35] Daniel: Great, we have a hard requirement that EU customer data must be stored and processed in the EU unless explicitly consented. There are a few legacy services that we allow cross-border for legal review but prefer to avoid.
[00:50] Alex: Understood. Redwood supports region pinning — we can pin inference and storage to specific regions, and we have dedicated EU capacity as an option. The key tradeoffs are cost and sometimes latency/throughput depending on capacity.
[01:10] Samir: When you say "pinning" is that all data, including logs, telemetry, and debug traces? We need audit logs to stay in-region too.
[01:25] Priya: Good question. We can configure retention and storage location for primary inference data and for audit logs. By default logs for debugging and metrics are stored in the same region as the customer dataset for dedicated deployments; for hosted we have region-affinity but some auxiliary logs may route to centralized services — we can enable EU-only logging for EU-dedicated.
[01:50] Jenna: Can you explain how the fallback works? If EU capacity is saturated and a request routes to a US node, is that automatic?
[02:05] Priya: We support routing policies. By default we route to pinned region; if capacity is full you can pick behavior: fail closed, queue, or fallback to a compatible model in another region. For FinEdge given legal constraints we'd recommend queueing or fail closed; fallback across border would be a cross-border processing event and we need explicit consent.
[02:30] Daniel: Yes, cross-border is a no-go without paperwork. We need a formal policy and an exception process.
[02:40] Alex: Noted. We'll share the region-pinning design doc and include explicit exception handling and audit trails for any cross-border events.
[03:00] Marta: On encryption — we use customer-managed keys, we need assurance keys never leave region. How does Redwood's KMS integration work?
[03:15] Priya: We support KMS integrations in a couple ways: hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS where keys are region-scoped; for Private/VPC and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) with either cloud KMS or HSM. In those cases keys live in your cloud project/region and Redwood's control plane does not have plaintext access.
[03:40] Daniel: So if we use our own KMS in EU region, there will be no key material transfer to US?
[03:50] Priya: Correct — key ops remain in-region. We only receive encrypted artifacts. For crypto ops we use an envelope encryption approach and the decryption occurs only on nodes with access to the KMS endpoint — which can be in the EU.
[04:10] Samir: What about subprocessors — do you have a list and do any of them process content outside the EU?
[04:20] Alex: We have a subprocessors list, we will share the latest csv. Most infra partners are global cloud providers (AWS, GCP) and some monitoring/observability partners may have cross-region dependencies; we can flag EU-only partners and offer dedicated capacity to limit exposure.
[04:40] Daniel: Please send that list. We also need contractual commitments around subprocessors and a subprocessor notification process.
[04:50] Alex: Absolutely, we'll include that in the next packet (SOC2 + subs).
[05:00] Marta: About RBAC/SSO — we have strict least privilege. Can you map Redwood roles to our SSO groups?
[05:10] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports SAML/SCIM provisioning for SSO; RBAC is configurable and you can map SAML groups to RBAC roles. We also support per-route or per-model access controls and token scoping for production vs dev.
[05:30] Jenna: Is there an audit log for admin actions? We need a record of who changed pinning policies or who spun up dedicated capacity.
[05:40] Priya: Yes, admin audit logs are captured and can be retained for configurable periods; they can be exported to your SIEM in-region if you want.
[05:55] Daniel: Retention periods — what's the default and can we set custom?
[06:05] Alex: Default 90 days for detailed traces, 365 for summarized logs. For enterprise we can extend retention and parity with your policy — that would be part of Dedicated or Private contract.
[06:20] Samir: About certifications — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001?
[06:25] Alex: Yes we have both; we'll attach the certs and the SOC2 bridge letter. Note that some redactions apply; we'll provide a summary plus full reports under NDA if needed.
[06:40] Samir: NDA seems likely, we'll follow up.
[06:45] Marta: Technical deep-dive question — how do you maintain data locality for long-running KV cache and prefix caching? If a customer has sessions that persist, how are they pinned?
[07:00] Priya: Caches are stored on the serving nodes and in optional in-region caches; for Dedicated we provision node pools in EU that maintain KV cache locality. For hosted we use smart routing to send session traffic to the same region and node pool; we also support sticky routing keys to preserve locality across requests.
[07:25] Daniel: If a node fails, does failover cause data to move cross-border?
[07:30] Priya: Failover respects region pinning. For catastrophic region failure we have outage policies; you can choose to fail closed to avoid cross-border processing. We will document RTO/RPO for region scenarios in the design doc.
[07:50] Alex: I'll also call out that Dedicated EU capacity gives you a stronger SLA and control; it's more expensive than vanilla hosted but meets stricter residency requirements.
[08:05] Jenna: What's the pricing delta roughly?
[08:10] Alex: Ballpark 1.6-2x depending on committed usage and instance types; we'll provide a tailored quote for FinEdge usage pattern.
[08:20] Marta: One more compliance ask — we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest details, plus key rotation policies.
[08:30] Priya: Everything is TLS1.2+ in transit, at rest is AES-256 with envelope encryption. Key rotation policies supported; you can schedule rotations or trigger them via KMS. We'll include rotation and scoping details in the artifact packet.
[08:50] Daniel: For cross-border exceptions, we need an audit trail and a whitelist of authorized personnel to approve. Can Redwood surface an approval workflow or is that on our side?
[09:05] Alex: We don't currently ship a full approval workflow productized but we can integrate with your ticketing/approval system and create a flagged event with required approvers; we'll also add an audit flag in logs. Priya can show an example in the architecture doc.
[09:25] Priya: I'll add a sample workflow diagram.
[09:30] Samir: Any subprocessors in the US doing inference?
[09:35] Alex: Not for EU-dedicated if you opt into it. For global hosted customers some inference helpers (model optimization tooling) might live elsewhere; again we can restrict those or move them into EU for dedicated deals.
[09:55] Jenna: How about backup copies / snapshots — where are they stored?
[10:00] Priya: Snapshots are stored in-region by default for dedicated; for hosted they follow region-affinity but backups to secondary regions can be disabled. We'll document backup geography and retention controls.
[10:20] Daniel: Ok, good. A couple of nitty-gritty items — Do you process logs via any third-party analytics that might export out of EU?
[10:30] Alex: We use a mix of home-grown and third-party observability. For EU-only deployments we can configure observability to use EU-only partners; we'll provide a mapping of which partner processes what data.
[10:45] Marta: Network egress — do you have any hard-coded egress to US endpoints for telemetry?
[10:50] Priya: No hard-coded egress; endpoints are region-scoped. There are optional centralized control-plane calls (control plane is multi-region) but sensitive data is not sent there — control plane metadata only. We'll be explicit in the doc about what is sent to the control plane.
[11:10] Alex: Quick note, transcription may not be perfect — apologies if names are fuzzy in the automated transcript.
[11:20] Daniel: All good. For legal: we'd like a subprocessors contractual clause and notification timeline.
[11:30] Samir: Typically 30 day notice is ok; for critical subprocessors we want 60 day notice and right to object.
[11:40] Alex: We'll propose 30/60 templates and highlight any critical subprocessors.
[11:50] Marta: Can we see an architecture sketch mapping requests from EU customers to EU-serving nodes?
[11:55] Priya: Yes, I'll attach the sketch. It will show routing, KMS flow, and fallback behavior.
[12:05] Jenna: Any available benchmarks for latency in EU-dedicated vs hosted?
[12:10] Priya: We have perf profiles for model families and can run a short benchmark using FinEdge's sample prompts; SE-led bench takes about a week to run and we can run it in EU region.
[12:25] Daniel: We'll supply sample prompts and traffic patterns.
[12:30] Alex: Great. Recap of agreed next steps — Alex will share SOC2/ISO and subprocessors list, Priya will send region-pinning diagram and sample workflow for cross-border exceptions, and we'll schedule a VPC deep-dive and a benchmarking run.
[12:50] Samir: Sounds good. Also please include contact for incident response and our legal team will coordinate NDA if needed.
[13:00] Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone for your time.
[13:05] Marta: Thanks.
[13:10] Meeting end.
